article.summary: Decision Keeper is an instruction-and-skill workflow for storing project decisions as Markdown under docs/decision/. It installs client-specific guidance and asks the host agent to recognize, retrieve, apply, and organize lasting project rules. The reviewed repository does not provide a separate memory service or structured record API.

who_what.text: The catalog places Decision Keeper at ordinal 181, uses slug decision-keeper and lists the explicit locator https://github.com/mudassirzulfiqar/Decision-Keeper. The pinned Atlas report is retained only for identity and locator attribution.

The official public GitHub repository is mudassirzulfiqar/Decision-Keeper, its default branch is main, and official branch metadata plus a shallow checkout agree on full head 911ff6b88e7c5e65b64326f9a5719291e6608ab6.
The README describes a Markdown decision knowledge base installed into Codex or Claude Code projects; the skill defines the agent-mediated capture, read, apply and organize workflow.
The official pinned README publishes no contact email; contact_email is null and the exact checked README URL is recorded.

architecture.text: The installer appends managed instructions and copies client-specific skill files; the README documents shared project decision files under docs/decision/ for Codex and Claude Code.

The memory unit is a Markdown rule or reusable correction organized in an index and linked topic files. The skill directs a full index read followed by relevant linked reads; the reviewed source provides no typed record schema, database, identifiers or retrieval index.

The installer checks root selection, symlink paths and recognized file hashes before writing. The bundled organizer specifies one active rule per bullet and a ten-rule file limit; its checker reports broken links, duplicates, orphan files and over-limit topics. These checks validate tree structure, while decision recognition and application still rely on the host agent.

The bundled organizer and checker provide concrete organization and structural validation, but they do not judge factual correctness, confirmation provenance, policy scope, or whether the host agent actually applied a rule. The checker is invoked by the organizer procedure rather than continuously.

behavior.text: Write: capture clear lasting user-confirmed rules and reusable corrections, skip one-off or tentative content, and allow explicit /keep and /keep and go triggers. The skill tells the agent to omit secrets, personal data and transcripts.

Update: apply rules at the narrowest supported scope, preserve unchanged parts of a choice, and resolve material conflicts before recording a new default. The reviewed implementation surface is prose-guided Markdown editing, not a typed correction API.
Delete: README and skill describe dropping/removing a rule. No delete API, tombstone, mutation ledger or cross-copy retention guarantee is defined in the inspected files.
Retrieval: read the project decision index in full and follow relevant topic links. This is instruction-based file retrieval with no ranking algorithm or measured accuracy.

Scope: installation is project-root based and the skill requires opt-in project instructions. The installer refuses filesystem root/home and nested Git subdirectories. These boundaries do not constitute per-user or tenant authorization on later operations.

Provenance: the workflow asks for user-confirmed rules and marks manual triggers as manual entries, but the Markdown model has no required author, timestamp, source passage, confidence, trust state or audit history fields.

Efficiency and observability: ordinary Markdown avoids a required database, but full-index reading can increase context cost with tree size. No indexing, background processing, telemetry, usage accounting or performance data is present in reviewed files.
No runtime, tests or benchmark workloads were run; all project metric domains remain unmeasured.

limits.text: The reviewed repository is a small instruction and skill package rather than a standalone memory runtime; its behavior depends on host-agent interpretation and project files.

The organizer and checker provide deterministic file-organization rules and structural checks, but they do not validate whether a decision is true, user-confirmed, correctly scoped, or applied by the host agent. The checker is only useful when the workflow invokes it.

No structured provenance or mutation history is guaranteed by the documented Markdown data model. Git history may retain edits, but repository-specific retention and privacy behavior are outside this source review.
The read-all-index instruction favors predictable inspection but can scale poorly in prompt/context use as project decision files grow; no measured limits or optimization are documented.
No Decision Keeper runtime, tests or benchmarks were run; all metric domains are unmeasured.
